title: Measuring the monetization strategies of websites with application to pro- and anti-vaccine communities
screen_reason: The paper's aim is to measure website monetization, but in characterising what pro- and anti-vaccine Facebook venues link to it reports observed shares of shared domains rated unreliable by source-credibility lists (GDI Dynamic Exclusion List and ref 30): 'Roughly 0.2% of the domains shared by pro-vaccine venues were rated as unreliable compared to roughly 50% for anti-vaccine venues.' That is a share of shared links carrying unreliable sources from platform data, i.e. SHARING, so the paper is eligible under the rule that a study whose aim is something else still counts if a descriptive share is reported. All the monetization measures themselves are outside the review's constructs.

estimates.country: not stated; venues and domains 'primarily written in English'
estimates.platform: Facebook (public groups/pages) linking out to web domains
estimates.date: venues identified November 2020; links/domains shared November 2019 to August 2021
estimates.measure_type: % of the distinct web domains shared by anti-vaccine Facebook venues that are rated unreliable by source-credibility organisations
estimates.value_raw: roughly 50% for anti-vaccine venues (no numerator or per-group denominator printed; read from Fig. 3)
estimates.denominator: the distinct web domains shared in posts by 261 anti-vaccine Facebook groups/pages between November 2019 and August 2021 (per-group domain count not reported; 2,436 distinct domains across all 451 pro- and anti-vaccine venues, from 46,472 unique shared URLs)
estimates.definition: A shared domain counted in the numerator if a source-credibility organisation rated it unreliable - a binary rating from the Global Disinformation Index's Dynamic Exclusion List and the list in ref 30
estimates.misinfo_def: The paper gives no formal definition of misinformation; it operationalises it at source level as domains 'rated as unreliable' by credibility organisations, in a study framed around "Anti-vaccine content and other kinds of misinformation"
estimates.n: distinct domains shared by 261 anti-vaccine venues (count not reported)
estimates.source_quote: We find that anti-vaccine Facebook venues share a much higher proportion of links to unreliable information sources (Fig. 3). Roughly 0.2% of the domains shared by pro-vaccine venues were rated as unreliable compared to roughly 50% for anti-vaccine venues.
estimates.page_loc: Results, p. 4 (final paragraph before Discussion); Fig. 3
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Binary site-credibility measures from the Global Disinformation Index (GDI) Dynamic Exclusion List and the list in ref 30; news/non-news classification and three continuous credibility scales (Ad Fontes Media, professional fact-checkers, Media Bias/Fact-Check) taken from ref 29. Venue labelling (pro- vs anti-vaccine) was manual with Cohen's kappa = 0.88 (95% CI 0.85-0.92). No reliability figure applies to the domain ratings themselves, which are third-party lists.
estimates.moderator_quote: In November 2020, we identified vaccine-related Facebook groups/pages as described in27 based on whether they mentioned vaccine-related terms ("vaccine", "vaxx", "vaccines", "jab", etc.)-at least once. ... These groups/pages were manually annotated as either pro-vaccine, anti-vaccine, or other. (Cohen's k = 0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.92). From the 451 groups/pages, we extracted 46,472 unique URLs shared in their posts. These URLs belonged to 2436 distinct domains.
estimates.notes: IMPORTANT for pooling: the unit is the DISTINCT DOMAIN, not the link or the share, so this is an unweighted repertoire share - a domain shared once counts the same as one shared thousands of times. It is therefore not comparable with volume-weighted 'share of shared links that were unreliable' estimates. The value is the authors' own approximation ('roughly 50%') of a figure, with no numerator and no per-group denominator printed anywhere, hence confidence low. Population is a purposively identified anti-vaccine community, not a general population.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, with reasons: (a) All four monetization measures and their shares (98% of domains display some monetization; 96-98% dedicate space to ads; Table 1: ad count 1,588/65.22%, donation count 1,978/81.23%, ad occupancy 2,353/98.45%, outbound links 2,141/89.96%; '95% using more than one'; medians such as 0.51 vs 2.73 ads) - monetization is not misinformation prevalence, so these fall outside every construct in the schema. (b) 'Roughly 88% of the links shared in pro-vaccine venues are to news sites, compared to roughly 67% for anti-vaccine venues' - a news/non-news composition share, not a falsity or unreliability share. (c) The three continuous credibility distributions in Fig. 4 (Ad Fontes Media, fact-checkers, Media Bias/Fact-Check) - reported only as medians and distributional shapes in a figure, with no share of domains below any threshold, so no derivable share (a scale reported without a share yields no row). (d) '58% of sites appeal for donations' - a figure the paper cites from ref 25 (Herasimenka et al.), excluded per R8. (e) The 261/190 venue counts and 412,168 URL counts are denominators for the monetization work, not for the unreliability shares. FOR THE ADJUDICATOR, two internal inconsistencies in the domain denominator: the Methods say the 46,472 shared URLs 'belonged to 2436 distinct domains' and Table 2 lists 2,435 / 2,390 / 2,380 domains per measure, but the Discussion says 'Nearly all 4619 domains in our sample' - 2,436 versus 4,619 is unreconciled in the text. Also, the venue total is given as 451 groups/pages while 190 pro + 261 anti = 451 exactly, so no venues labelled 'other' survive into Table 2 despite 'other' being an annotation option. Neither issue changes the extracted percentages, but both mean the denominators behind Fig. 3 cannot be reconstructed from the paper.

rob.design: Observational two-stage design on CrowdTangle Facebook data. Stage 1: vaccine-related Facebook groups/pages identified in November 2020 by vaccine keywords with animal-vaccine keywords excluded and a >=20% vaccine-post or vaccine-in-name filter, leaving 451 venues manually annotated pro- / anti- / other-vaccine (Cohen's kappa 0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.92); 190 pro and 261 anti retained. Stage 2: 46,472 unique URLs shared by those venues, reduced to 2,436 distinct domains (chosen over URLs because of takedowns and link rot); for each domain all articles posted November 2019-August 2021 were crawled, giving 412,168 URLs for HTML measures, with stratified subsamples of 29,713 (ad occupancy) and 30,816 (outbound links) live pages. Unreliability was assigned at domain level from third-party lists (GDI Dynamic Exclusion List, ref 30) and news/non-news and continuous credibility from ref 29. Comparisons by two-tailed Mann-Whitney U. Limitations stated by the authors: a point-in-time snapshot, no revenue data, English-language venues and domains only. Limitations for prevalence use: no numerator or per-arm denominator for the unreliability shares, distinct-domain rather than volume-weighted unit, and CrowdTangle data are not publicly redistributable.
